why: With kdoc forced false in the indent choice, a wrapped KDoc line (addKdoc text containing ♢ on a member at indent>0) gets indentLevel+2 instead of indentLevel; only the file-comment wrap case is tested.
Wrapped KDoc lines would lose their ' * ' prefix (kdoc falls through to '' since comment is false); no test wraps a KDoc line through CodeWriter.
Only differs for an import key starting with '.', which adds "" to memberImportNames, but that set is only probed with ClassName.canonicalName, which is never empty.
LineWrapper.append("♢x") on a fresh line leaves segments ["", "x"]: original hasPendingSegments is true, mutant false, so a direct LineWrapper test (or indent("") body starting with ♢) exposes it.
For a digit after the first char (e.g. newName("a1")) the mutant inserts '_' giving "a_1" instead of "a1"; tests only cover a leading digit.
No production caller passes a fifth argument, but isOneOf is an internal utility whose signature accepts t5, and a direct test like 5.isOneOf(1,2,3,4,5) would kill it.
No production caller passes a sixth argument, but a direct call like 6.isOneOf(1,2,3,4,5,6) returns true originally and false under the mutant; nothing tests it.
With that branch disabled, '"' falls through to the else branch c.toString(), which returns the same "\"" string.

failIfEscapeInvalid can never throw on the chain's output: every illegal character is a non-identifier part, so escapeIfNotJavaIdentifier already backticks the string, and alreadyEscaped() then passes.
Flipping validate has no effect because failIfEscapeInvalid never throws on escapeIfNecessary output (any illegal char forces backtick escaping first).
Removing failIfEscapeInvalid is unobservable because its require can never fail on the already-escaped result of the preceding chain.
A string made only of underscores cannot start or end with a backtick, so !alreadyEscaped() is always true when allCharactersAreUnderscore holds.
Including the first char is harmless: it is either not an identifier start (the left operand is already true) or an identifier start, and every start char is also an identifier part.
replaceAll uses a literal String.replace of "[⇥|⇤]", which can never match because the parser always splits ⇥/⇤ into their own single-char format parts, so the map is a no-op.
Applying replaceAll to non-inline members is a no-op because the literal "[⇥|⇤]" never occurs in any format part.
Skipping replaceAll for inline annotations changes nothing because the literal-string replace of "[⇥|⇤]" never matches a format part.
Any single-char last format part now counts as a placeholder: addKdoc("See %L.", "foo") gives kdoc "See foo\n." instead of "See foo.\n" under ensureEndsWithNewLine.
isPlaceholder's only caller applies it to trim().formatParts.last(), and trim() strips trailing ⇥⇤«», so the first disjunct is always false anyway.
Format parts starting with ⇥/⇤/«/» are always exactly one char, so length!=1 && isSingleChar is always false, as is the original disjunct after trim().

Parts beginning with a single-char placeholder are always length 1 and are removed by trim(), and an empty last part (the only case where first() would throw) is never fed back into trimTrailingNewLine.
Equivalent to treating any length-1 last part as a placeholder, so kdoc like addKdoc("See %L.", "foo") gets its newline appended to the arg instead ("See foo\n.").
Parts beginning with '%' are always exactly two chars ("%L", "%%", ...) and text parts never contain '%', so dropping length==2 changes nothing on reachable parts.
Only an import key starting with '.' differs, adding "" to memberImportNames, which is only checked against non-empty ClassName canonical names.
A class with a property/function before a nested typealias, or with two typealiases, would lose the blank separator line; the only test has a lone typealias.

For a body like "return 1
«a
»%L
»c" (the %L arg CodeBlock supplies the extra «), the original sees an unmatched » and keeps a block body, while the mutant never returns true and emits an expression body; valid statement nesting otherwise makes it equivalent.

Once a « is seen, the counter never returns to 0, so an unmatched » after a matched pair (e.g. parts "return 1\n",«,a,»,%L,»,c with the arg providing «) is missed; it only diverges with statement brackets split across arg CodeBlocks.

Always appending Any? makes a bounded KTypeParameter such as <T : Number> (or an unbounded one) carry two bounds, changing bounds/equality and emitting a where-clause; no test checks KTypeParameter bounds.
For <T : Any> the reflected bounds become empty instead of [Any?], so asTypeVariableName() no longer equals TypeVariableName("T") and has empty bounds; untested.
parentSubcommandsVarName is only used inside the !isTopLevel branch, so what it holds for a top-level command is never observed (and computing it on empty parentNames doesn't throw).
A subcommand whose help contains an apostrophe would print it unescaped inside -d '...'; the fish tests never give subcommands help text.
A subcommand with non-blank help would lose its -d '...' description; the fish tests only use subcommands without help.
A command with no dash-named options (e.g. help option disabled, arguments only) would print an empty "## Options for" header.
An option with only non-dash names (e.g. "/o" or "+x", which clikt allows) would produce a bare "complete -c c" line instead of being skipped.
A single-dash multi-char option like "-foo" would be emitted with -s instead of -o; no fish test has such a name.
An argument with help text would lose its -d '...' in the fish output; the tested arguments have no help.
UsageError.paramName is a public var, so setting it to null on a NoSuchOption and formatting the message would NPE under the mutant instead of using ""; clikt itself never nulls it.
With a styling formatter (e.g. MordantHelpFormatter or a custom styleOptionName), the "did you mean" suggestions would appear unstyled; tests use the identity formatter or don't check it.
If the parent has --foo and a subcommand has --fob, typing --fob to the parent gives typo suggestions originally but the subcommand hint under the mutant.
An unknown option that no subcommand defines would wrongly get the "option belongs to subcommand X" hint, because every subcommand has a non-matching option such as --help.
SuspendingCompletionCommand's default or custom help text would vanish from parent help listings and completion descriptions; nothing asserts it.
Running SuspendingCompletionCommand as a root command (no parent context) would throw an NPE instead of generating completion for itself.
ChainedCompletionCommand's help text would become empty in parent help listings and fish -d descriptions; untested.
Running ChainedCompletionCommand as the root command would NPE instead of generating completion for itself.
